key_findings: **Application init identified**: FUN_0057A3C0 (1909 bytes) is the SOLE creator of the GameEngine singleton. It is a `__thiscall` method on a SERVICE CONTAINER object (param_1) that holds GameEngine as its first service (`*param_1`) plus 14+ more services as `param_1[1..0xD]`. 3 upstream callers (FUN_004DAF00, FUN_004DC690, FUN_004D7A60) represent different app-mode entries (new game / load / reload).

**6-layer binder chain mapped**: application init -> LuaClassRegistry init (BCS-Y-1521) -> mass class registry (BCS-Y-1738) -> per-class trampolines (FUN_00CC9700 / FUN_00CC9760) -> registration cores (FUN_00CD9F30 / FUN_00CDA610) -> class-table maintainer (FUN_00CD5620) -> LuaClassTable_find_or_create (BCS-Y-1670). The +0x1BC write happens within the FUN_00CD5620 chain (deepest layer not yet decompiled).

**Init order enforced**: GameEngine is created BEFORE the LuaClassRegistry init runs. So by the time any cc7000 cluster caller fires (the 23 consumers of FUN_00CD7A30 the +0x1BC reader), the binder has already populated +0x1BC. This explains why no race condition / null check is needed at the consumer side.

**GameEngine is a true singleton**: FUN_00CC9540 (the factory) has ONLY 1 caller, FUN_0057A3C0. There is no path to create multiple GameEngine instances; the engine lifecycle is bound to the application's service container lifecycle.

**Registration cores are bifurcated** (BaseClass-style vs LGTC-style) per the classification of the 36 classes (24 BaseClass + 12 LGTC). Each class goes through ONE of the two cores depending on its inheritance pattern - the LGTC core is for classes with the LGTC inheritance chain ( narratives).
